opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000; will only exceptionally exceed £6,000; travel up to £2,000 per person (trips ≤13 days) or £2,500 per person (14+ days); PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more up to £5,000; Japan office up to ¥300,000 for PhD students

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects (though the UK office may consider individuals with proof of organisational support). Payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts. Welcomes previous recipients. Projects originating in the UK apply via UK office, those in Japan via Japan office.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding to enable UK-Japan projects that might otherwise not be possible, bringing people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, exchange ideas/expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, teaching of Japanese language/cultural studies, and academic research/visits. Does not fund consumables, salaries, materials, capital projects, student fees, undergraduate/master's students, or retrospective activity.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December (annual, for a decision in March of the following year; prior to 2026 the deadline was 15 December)

amount.raw: up to £10,000; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally be able to show an existing research record, though consideration is also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. The project must involve partners in both the UK and Japan, and be supported by reputable referees not based at the same institution as either project partner. Preference to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants. Apply to the UK (London) office regardless of location.
opportunities.summary: Supports exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare. Creates opportunities for researchers, practitioners, policy makers, managers and voluntary sector workers to share knowledge and develop new approaches. May be used for travel, conference and publication costs. Cannot be used for laboratory consumables, salary subsidy, materials, capital projects, or retrospective activity.
